{
  "segment_function": "Examine the classical view of slavery and labor in antiquity, the Greek exclusion of labor from the human sphere, and the modern elevation of the animal laborans.",
  "claims": [
    {
      "claim": "In antiquity, labor and work were not despised simply because only slaves engaged in them; rather, ancients felt it necessary to own slaves because of the slavish nature of all occupations serving life's necessities.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The opinion that labor and work were despised in antiquity because only slaves engaged in them is a prejudice of modern historians. The ancients reasoned the other way around and felt it necessary to possess slaves because of the slavish nature of all occupations that served the needs for the maintenance of life.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [],
      "confidence": 1.0
    },
    {
      "claim": "The ancient institution of slavery was not designed as cheap labor or profit exploitation, but as an attempt to exclude labor from the conditions of human life.",
      "claim_type": "author_position",
      "supporting_excerpt": "The institution of slavery in antiquity, though not in later times, was not a device for cheap labor or an instrument of exploitation for profit but rather the attempt to exclude labor from the conditions of man’s life.",
      "support_kind": "direct",
      "qualifications": [
        "applies to antiquity, though not to later times"
      ],
      "confidence": 1.0
    }
  ],
  "definitions": [],
  "distinctions": [],
  "examples": [],

  ]
}
